artworks.title: The Golden Age
artworks.description: Oslo Nasjonalmuseet: Cranach's enclosed paradise of ease and play — Hesiod's first race remembered as a garden before silver and iron.

artworks.title: The Close of the Silver Age (?)
artworks.description: National Gallery, London: Cranach's quarreling nude race — the Silver Age tipping from soft living into the violence that ends the second race.

artworks.title: The Bronze Age (L'Aage d'Airain)
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print from a Four Ages series: the Bronze Age as armed strife — Hesiod's ash-born warriors who destroy one another.

artworks.title: The Iron Age (Aetas Ferrea)
artworks.artist: Jan Collaert II (after Tobias Verhaecht; published by Philip Galle)
artworks.description: Engraved Iron Age: toil, war, and broken faith — the last race Hesiod says Zeus will destroy when even the newborn are grey.

popCulture.title: Ages of Man
popCulture.description: Hesiod's gold-to-iron descent remains the West's template for civilizational decline — five ages from ease to iron war.

popCulture.title: Works and Days
popCulture.creator: Hesiod
popCulture.description: Hesiod's poem that numbers the races — gold, silver, bronze, heroes, iron — and makes decline a moral calendar.
